text.p: Lebanon is preparing to issue mark-denominated bonds on the German financial markets, acting finance minister Fouad Siniora said on Monday.
"We have started negotiations with a number of financial institutions in Germany in preparation for issuing mark-denominated bonds," Siniora told Reuters in a telephone interview.

Siniora, who ended an official visit to Germany on Saturday, declined to give further information on the German institutions with which the Lebanese government was negotiating or on the size of the issue, its maturity and the interest it would carry.
"We are interested in issuing in the mark because the interest on this currency's bills is lower than that on the U.S. treasury bills," Siniora said.
"I don't want to go into details because we are still in the phase of negotiations," he added.
The interest rate on two-year German bills is currently 3.75 percent a year. It is 4.75 percent on five-year bonds, 7.125 percent on seven-year bonds and six percent on 10-year notes.
This compares with interest rates of 10.125 percent and 9.125 percent on Lebanon's first two dollar-denominated three-year and five-year eurobond issues in 1994 and 1995.
Yields on Lebanese pound-denominated t-bills currently range from 13.29 percent on three-month maturities to 16.08 percent on two-year maturities.
